goal: Turn cancelled literal-user confirmations into durable, resumable Kernel state instead of session-only pending payloads: cancelling any Assurance confirmation records exactly one unresolved_user_decision bound to the blocked operation, survives session restart, and resumes through the existing resolve-user-decision authority path with the identical operation.

acceptance.assertion: Every cancellable Assurance confirmation (record-review-verdict, record-review-approval, record-user-approval, stop, begin-drain, approve-breaking-intent-revision, and resolve-user-decision) is enumerated by trigger (user cancel, timeout, session shutdown) crossed with state (pending, applied, superseded) with a single decision-trail owner per state; a cancel before application records exactly one unresolved_user_decision bound to the exact operation and snapshot digest without applying the underlying verdict or approval; repeated cancels deduplicate onto the same open decision; the pending payload is durable Kernel state rather than Pi session memory and survives session restart; resolve-user-decision re-opens the identical operation for literal-user confirmation; and invocation tokens are released across terminal completion, cancellation, error, and session-shutdown exit paths.
Existing single-terminal settlement, deferred-rejection nonterminal ownership, and invocation lifecycle cleanup invariants remain intact under the new cancel path with zero automatic retries.
The complete Pi extension graph passes strict TypeScript checking and the full repository test suite passes with no regressions.
